lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The résumé has no summary or explicit target-role positioning.
items.because: Recruiters must infer whether the target is ML engineering, applied science, LLM engineering, or agent infrastructure.

items.says: The engineering narrative does not prioritize one dominant technical profile.
items.because: The résumé supports four interpretations, making the target unclear without prioritization.

items.says: The strongest ML and agent achievements are not consistently ordered first.
items.because: Recruiters often read only the first one or two bullets under each position.

items.says: The boundaries among several evaluation and reliability claims are unclear.
items.because: They may describe related work, reducing perceived breadth and raising duplication concerns.

items.says: The code portfolio should be checked for relevant, accessible evidence or removed.
items.because: An empty, private, or unrelated repository weakens credibility.

items.says: The date of birth should be deleted.
items.because: It is irrelevant to hiring and creates age-discrimination and privacy concerns.

items.says: Nationality should be removed unless a specific application requires it.
items.because: It is generally not useful on a North American technical résumé, and work authorization should be stated separately when relevant.

items.says: The graduate degree lacks relevant coursework, research, or specialization context.
items.because: The résumé does not show what the graduate specialization contributes to the target role.

items.says: The expected status should be made visually unmistakable.
items.because: Recruiters may otherwise misread the degree as completed.

items.says: The 35% diagnostic-accuracy improvement lacks a clear metric definition, baseline, and evaluation setting.
items.because: Diagnostic accuracy could mean absolute percentage points, relative improvement, or a particular classification metric.

items.says: The description of validated trajectories and assistant-only loss masking is too dense and does not show which part produced the improvement.
items.because: Recruiters may not understand the cause, while technical reviewers will want the training and evaluation details.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking is repeated in another bullet.
items.because: Repeated methods make the résumé appear padded and reduce space for differentiated work.

items.says: The operational purpose of the routing layer is unclear.
items.because: The reader needs to understand what reliability or workflow problem the routing solved.

items.says: The meaning of reviewer disagreement is not defined.
items.because: It could refer to false positives, conflicting diagnoses, invalid tool outputs, or another reliability measure.

items.says: The relationship among the three specialists, reviewer, and input signals is hard to follow.
items.because: The reader must reconstruct the system architecture from the current phrasing.

items.says: The GRPO comparison lacks dataset size, statistical comparability, and production-versus-offline conditions.
items.because: Those evaluation conditions are needed to make the efficiency and equal-accuracy claims credible.

items.says: GRPO is presented too prominently relative to the system-level result.
items.because: Recruiters may treat algorithm names as buzzwords, while reduced tool use and latency without accuracy loss are the real value.

items.says: The consequence of catching the two regressions is not fully stated.
items.because: The bullet does not establish whether the regressions were prevented from reaching release or production.

items.says: The ownership level for the evaluation harness is unclear.
items.because: It matters whether the candidate owned the harness and methodology or implemented part of a larger system.

items.says: This bullet repeats assistant-only loss masking from the earlier fine-tuning bullet.
items.because: It adds no new outcome and makes the résumé appear padded.

items.says: If this was a separate experiment, it lacks a distinct result.
items.because: Methods without a separate measurable outcome are weaker than achievements with impact.

items.says: The diagnostics triage and backlog-reduction achievement is duplicated in Projects.
items.because: The overlap raises questions about which team owned the work and where the result occurred.

items.says: The 68% backlog reduction lacks an unambiguous baseline and operational significance.
items.because: The eight-week period is helpful, but the comparison point still needs clarification.

items.says: The BF16 memory reduction does not state what it enabled.
items.because: The reader needs the practical consequence, such as larger batches, fewer out-of-memory failures, lower cost, or faster training.

items.says: The 4x figure does not specify what kind of GPU memory was measured.
items.because: Clarifying peak, allocated, or another memory measurement would improve credibility.

items.says: The p95 latency comparison does not confirm equivalent workload and traffic conditions.
items.because: Latency comparisons are meaningful only under comparable load and test conditions.

items.says: The build-failure safeguard needs confirmation that it was actually enforced in CI.
items.because: It is a strong reliability signal only if it was automated and routinely used.

items.says: The CI bullet has a grammar and tense inconsistency in “Maintained” and “adds.”
items.because: The shift from past tense to present-tense third person reads like an editing error.

items.says: The meaning of “release cycles to 3 days” is ambiguous.
items.because: It could mean three days from code completion to release or a reduction to a three-day cycle.

items.says: The release-cycle result lacks a prior baseline or release count.
items.because: The impact is difficult to assess without a comparison point.

items.says: The operational result of the event-queue migration could be more precise.
items.because: The outcome should show more specifically how the architecture improved failures, backlog, dispatch reliability, or manual intervention.

items.says: Ownership of the migration across 30 services is unclear.
items.because: The wording should accurately distinguish leading, implementing, or contributing to a team effort.

items.says: The “dead-letter handling” phrase has a line-break artifact that should be fixed.
items.because: PDF or source-formatting hyphenation should not appear as an awkward split.

items.says: The AI-first engineering-practices bullet is vague and unsupported.
items.because: “Drove adoption,” “accelerating delivery,” and “improving outcomes” are broad claims without measurable evidence.

items.says: The meaning of “raw conversation grew 100x” and the capability preserved are unclear.
items.because: The reader needs to know what grew and what functionality remained intact.

items.says: The bullet does not state what the context-management design enabled.
items.because: Cost control, stable latency, successful task completion, or avoidance of context-window failure matters more than the implementation technique alone.

items.says: The stress test is not shown to be representative of realistic workloads.
items.because: A technical reviewer may question whether it used realistic tool calls, message sizes, and workloads.

items.says: The conditions that caused the deadlocks and lost results are not stated.
items.because: Concise failure conditions would make the systems diagnosis more informative.

items.says: The meaning of 50-way fan-out is unclear.
items.because: It could be a tested upper bound, production workload, or stress-test configuration.

items.says: The reliability or throughput improvement is not quantified.
items.because: Measured successful completion or throughput would make the result more compelling.

items.says: “Integrated” does not identify the specific nature of the contribution.
items.because: A technical reviewer will want to know whether the work covered implementation, metric adaptation, testing, API design, or framework integration.

items.says: The open-source contribution lacks a directly accessible project link.
items.because: Open-source work is a stronger credibility signal when reviewers can verify it.

items.says: The operational meaning of the 0.89 Kendall correlation is not explained.
items.because: Many readers will not immediately understand whether it shows correct ranking of degraded outputs or detection of quality loss.

items.says: The unit and source of the 400-plus trials need more clarity.
items.because: The reader may want to know whether the reports were synthetic, human-authored, or production-like.

items.says: This diagnostics triage and backlog-reduction result duplicates the professional-experience achievement.
items.because: Counting the same accomplishment twice creates a credibility problem.

items.says: If this was separate work, its ownership, data, evaluation setting, or result is not distinguished.
items.because: Without those distinctions, it appears to be the same accomplishment.

items.says: Programming languages and the Git development tool are grouped together.
items.because: Languages, version control, and infrastructure tools signal different capabilities.

items.says: The skills list underrepresents the systems and evaluation capabilities demonstrated elsewhere.
items.because: Fine-tuning, tool-use systems, inference optimization, evaluation harnesses, CI/CD, caching, queues, and GPU optimization are among the résumé’s strongest supported themes.
